newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland may float up to 30 pct of KGHM in London.
newsitem.headline: Poland may float up to 30 pct of KGHM in London.

text.p: The board of Poland's KGHM copper concern and its privatisation advisers are considering doubling to 30 percent the amount of the firm to be floated on the London stock exchange, a KGHM official said.

Ireneusz Nawrocki, the head of KGHM's supervisory board, told Reuters on Wednesday the firm's employees would likely get 15 percent of the stock free and a yet undecided amount of shares would be sold on the Warsaw bourse in mid-1997.

"The board, working with the company's privatisation advisers, is currently considering the flotation of between 25 and 30 percent of KGHM's shares in London, but no decisions have been made yet," Nawrocki said.
"This is just one of the stages of planning the firm's sale...more details could be available in mid-February," he said.

In a tentative privatisation plan last year the government earmarked 15 percent of KGHM's shares for the London flotation, in the form of Global Depositary Receipts, and 10 percent for Warsaw, but said the final division would be made on the privatisation advisers' recommendation.
"The most important factor in determining the division of shares is the absorptiveness of the Warsaw bourse at the planned time of flotation," Nawrocki said.

Apart from KGHM, Poland also wants to float several other big companies this year such as Bank Handlowy, Telekomunikcja Polska SA, Ciech chemicals trader and Petrochemia Plock SA, raising doubts concerns among analysts' over whether the capital market will be deep enough to absorb the offers.
KGHM, estimated to be worth some $2-$3 billion, is one of the world's largest copper and silver producers.
KGHM's privatisation adviser is a consortium of Union Bank of Switzerland, Barclays de Zoete Wedd and Wielkopolski Bank Kreydtowy SA brokerage.
